kg.node.mbd2_event_on_load.desc.1: Runs one tick after the block entity becomes valid, not during load itself - so the level, the machine's traits and its neighbours are all readable by the time it fires.
kg.node.mbd2_event_on_load.desc.2: Server-side only. For one-off setup that both sides need, write it to custom data here and read it from Custom Data Updated on the client.
kg.node.mbd2_event_tick.desc.1: The main hook for anything periodic. It fires before the recipe logic runs, so cancelling it stops the machine's entire tick - recipe progress, trait ticking and auto-IO included.
kg.node.mbd2_event_tick.desc.2: Fires every tick for every machine of this definition. Use Offset Timer with a modulo if the work only needs to happen occasionally; a hundred machines all doing it every tick is a hundred times the cost.
kg.node.mbd2_event_client_tick.desc.1: The client's own tick, with no server counterpart. Nothing done here is synced or saved, and the machine's traits hold whatever the last sync gave them.
kg.node.mbd2_event_client_tick.desc.2: Anything that changes world state belongs in Machine Tick instead - the machine action nodes refuse to run here for that reason.
kg.node.mbd2_event_placed.desc.1: Fires after the block entity exists, so the machine is fully readable. The placer may be absent when something other than a player placed it.
kg.node.mbd2_event_placed.desc.2: The stack still carries whatever data components the placed item had, which is how a machine can remember what it was crafted from.
kg.node.mbd2_event_removed.desc.1: Fires while the machine is still in the world and still readable. Its traits and custom data are intact at this point - after this they are gone.
kg.node.mbd2_event_removed.desc.2: For changing what drops, use Machine Drops instead; this one is for side effects elsewhere.
kg.node.mbd2_event_drops.desc.1: The list is the one the game will actually spawn, and it already contains the machine item and whatever the traits added.
kg.node.mbd2_event_drops.desc.2: Replace it with Set Machine Drops. Building a new list with the generic list nodes and leaving it there does nothing - the game never reads the value back off the event.
kg.node.mbd2_event_neighbor_changed.desc: Fires for any block change next to the machine, not just redstone - a neighbour being placed, broken or changing state all reach here.
The machine's own redstone reading is not updated for you; read it with Get Redstone Signal on the side you care about.
kg.node.mbd2_event_state_changed.desc.1: Fires before the change is applied, so the machine still reports the old state while this runs. That also means reading Machine State here gives oldState, not newState.
kg.node.mbd2_event_state_changed.desc.2: Cancelling keeps the machine where it is. Setting the state from inside this event re-enters it, so guard against a loop.
kg.node.mbd2_event_custom_data_update.de: Fires on both sides whenever the tag is replaced, which is what makes it the way to react to a server-side change on the client.
It fires on replacement, not on mutation - a blueprint that edits the tag in place will not trigger it. Use Set Custom Data or Merge Custom Data.
kg.node.mbd2_event_use_item_on.desc.1: Fires before the machine's own handling, so the outcome you set decides what happens next. Leaving it alone lets the machine open its UI as usual.
kg.node.mbd2_event_use_item_on.desc.2: Fires on both sides. Take the click on the server and return the same result on the client, or the player's hand will swing out of step with what actually happened.
kg.node.mbd2_event_use_without_item.desc: The empty-handed counterpart of Use Item On, with the same both-sides caveat: decide the same way on client and server.
This is the hook for a machine that should do something other than open its UI when clicked.
kg.node.mbd2_event_open_ui.desc.1: Server-side, and fires after the machine has already decided it has a UI to open. Cancelling is how a blueprint gates access - on ownership, on a redstone signal, on whatever it likes.
kg.node.mbd2_event_open_ui.desc.2: Cancelling here does not consume the click; the player just sees nothing happen.
kg.node.mbd2_event_ui.desc.1: Fires while the modular UI is being built, once per player who opens it. The UI handed over is the one from the machine's UI editor, before it is shown.
kg.node.mbd2_event_ui.desc.2: Client-side work only - the layout is not synced, so anything decided here has to be derivable from data the client already has.
kg.node.mbd2_event_use_catalyst.desc.1: Fires on a multiblock controller when a player uses a catalyst item to form it, before the pattern is checked.
kg.node.mbd2_event_use_catalyst.desc.2: Cancelling stops the structure forming, which is how a blueprint adds its own condition - a tier requirement, an unlock, a time of day.
kg.node.mbd2_event_before_recipe_working: Fires every tick a recipe runs, before progress advances. Cancelling holds the recipe exactly where it is rather than failing it, so the machine resumes when the condition clears.
This is the hook for a per-tick requirement the recipe itself does not express - a fuel the recipe type does not know about, a neighbouring block that has to stay put.
kg.node.mbd2_event_on_recipe_working.des: Fires every tick a recipe runs, with the progress it has reached, so it is the hook for anything that should scale with how far along the recipe is.
Progress is in ticks. Divide by the recipe's duration, or use Progress Percent on the recipe logic, for a 0..1 value.
The mirror of Before Recipe Working: it fires once progress has advanced, so the progress the recipe logic reports is already the new one.
Not cancelable - the tick has happened by the time this runs.
kg.node.mbd2_event_on_recipe_waiting.des: Fires every tick a matched recipe cannot proceed, which for a blocked machine means every tick indefinitely. Keep the work here small.
Read Waiting Reason on the recipe logic for what is blocking it.
kg.node.mbd2_event_on_recipe_finish.desc: Fires after the outputs have been produced, so the output slots already hold them.
The recipe handed over is the modified one the machine actually ran, not the one in the datapack. Compare against Origin Recipe Id if you need to know which recipe it started as.
kg.node.mbd2_event_on_consume_inputs_aft: Only fires for machines configured to consume inputs at the end of a recipe rather than the start.
The inputs are already gone by the time this runs.
kg.node.mbd2_event_recipe_status_changed: Fires on the transition, not every tick, which makes it the right place for one-off reactions - starting a sound, switching a machine state, emitting a redstone pulse.
Both the old and new status are given, so a blueprint can distinguish stopping from starting.
The main hook for changing what a recipe costs or produces. It fires before the definition's own recipe modifiers, so anything set here is what those modifiers then see.
The recipe handed over may be the shared instance the recipe manager holds. Never change it in place - build a copy with Copy Recipe or Scale Recipe and hand that to Set Event Recipe.
Cancelling rejects the recipe outright, which makes the machine look for another.
kg.node.mbd2_event_recipe_modify_after.d: Fires once the definition's modifiers have had their turn, so this is the last word on a recipe.
Same copy rule as Recipe Modify (Before): change a copy and write it back with Set Event Recipe.
kg.node.mbd2_event_fuel_recipe_modify.de: The fuel counterpart of Recipe Modify (Before), for machines whose recipe type burns fuel.
Change a copy and write it back with Set Event Recipe; cancel to reject the fuel.
kg.node.mbd2_event_fuel_burning_finish.d: Fires when a fuel recipe has burnt out, before the machine looks for the next one.
The recipe may be absent, so guard before reading it.
kg.node.mbd2_event_structure_formed.desc: Fires on the controller once the pattern matches, after the parts have been attached - so Multiblock Parts already returns them.
Server-side. For a client reaction, react to the machine state change instead.
kg.node.mbd2_event_structure_invalid.des: Fires when the structure breaks, before the parts are detached, so they are still readable here.
It also fires when the controller itself is removed.
Fires from the animation itself, on the client, when it passes a keyframe carrying a custom instruction. The instruction text is whatever the animation file put there.
Because it is client-side, this is for presentation - a sound, a particle - not for logic.
kg.node.mbd2_event_cancel.desc.1: Cancelling is the event's own business: a cancelled Machine Tick skips the whole tick, a cancelled Recipe Modify rejects the recipe, a cancelled Open UI keeps the UI shut. Events that are not cancelable ignore this.
kg.node.mbd2_event_cancel.desc.2: When several blueprints are attached, all of them run and any one may cancel. The cancel input exists so a later blueprint can also take a cancel back off.
kg.node.mbd2_event_set_recipe.desc.1: Only the three recipe-modify events read a recipe back off themselves; under anything else this does nothing.
kg.node.mbd2_event_set_recipe.desc.2: Leaving the input empty rejects the recipe, which has the same effect as cancelling.
kg.node.mbd2_event_set_item_interaction_: The machine sets PASS_TO_DEFAULT_BLOCK_INTERACTION before dispatch, so doing nothing lets its normal handling continue.
Set the same result on both sides. Deciding SUCCESS on the server and PASS on the client makes the player's arm swing disagree with what happened.
kg.node.mbd2_event_set_interaction_resul: The machine sets PASS before dispatch, so doing nothing lets it open its UI as usual.
Same both-sides rule as Set Item Interaction Result.
kg.node.mbd2_event_set_drops.desc.1: The list is replaced in place, because the machine hands the event its own list and never reads a replacement back. That is also why building a list with the generic nodes and not calling this does nothing.
kg.node.mbd2_event_set_drops.desc.2: Empty stacks are skipped, so a filtered list needs no cleanup first.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_info.desc.1: Wire the machine once here and stack as many property blocks inside as the graph needs, instead of running the same wire into a node per property.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_info.desc.2: With the target unwired it reads the blueprint's own machine, which is what almost every graph wants. Wire it to reach a neighbour found with Machine At Position, or a multiblock part.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_level.desc.1: Absent for a machine that is not in a world yet - during construction, or in the editor preview.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_pos.desc.1: The block position of the machine itself. For a multiblock part this is the part's position, not its controller's.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_block_state.desc.1: Read live from the world, so it reflects whatever the machine's state machine last applied.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_block_entity.desc.1: The bridge to KilaGraph's generic block-entity and world nodes, for anything the machine nodes do not cover.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_front_facing.desc.1: Flattened from the optional the machine returns, because the graph carries no optional direction and every consumer would handle the empty case the same way.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_front_facing.desc.2: Pair it with Has Front Facing when the difference between 'faces north' and 'has no facing' matters.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_has_front_facing.de: False for a machine whose definition gives it no facing - the case Front Facing reports as NORTH.
Stable across worlds and saves, so this is what to compare against when a blueprint has to know which machine it is on.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_definition.desc.1: The definition object, for the definition-level nodes. For just the id, use Definition Id.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_name.desc.1: The custom name if the machine has been renamed in an anvil, otherwise its block's name.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_drop_item.desc.1: The stack the machine would drop as, including its custom name. Not what it will actually drop - that is Machine Drops.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_state.desc.1: The state name, which is what the state machine, the renderer, the shape, the light level and the sound all key off.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_state.desc.2: Change it with Set Machine State; setting a name the definition does not declare is ignored.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_tier.desc.1: The dynamic override if one has been set, otherwise the tier the definition configures. Set it with Set Machine Tier.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_custom_data.desc.1: The machine's own persisted, synced tag - the place to keep blueprint state that has to survive a reload or reach the client.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_custom_data.desc.2: Read-only here. The tag is change-tracked by identity, so mutating this copy neither syncs nor fires Custom Data Updated; go through Set Custom Data or Merge Custom Data.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_is_remote.desc.1: True on the client. Client-side events do fire - Client Tick, the UI ones - so a blueprint that hooks both sides needs this to tell them apart.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_is_remote.desc.2: The machine action nodes already refuse to run on the client, so this is for the graph's own logic.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_offset_timer.desc.1: The world time plus a per-position offset, so machines at different positions land on different ticks.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_offset_timer.desc.2: Use it with a modulo to spread periodic work out: a hundred machines checking something every twenty ticks costs a twentieth of a hundred machines checking every tick. Every N Ticks is that pattern in a single block.
The staggered periodic tick, ready made: true once every interval ticks, and on a phase of this machine's own so a hundred of them do not all fire on the same tick.
Offset Timer into Modulo into Equals 0 does the same job by hand and gives the same answer. This block is the shorter way to write it, with the phase and the comparison kept in one place.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_recipe_logic.desc.1: The bridge to the recipe-logic nodes. Every machine has one, whether or not its definition gives it a recipe type.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_recipe_type.desc.1: The recipe type from the definition. Machines with no recipe logic report the dummy type.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_self.desc.1: The same machine every other machine node falls back to when its machine input is unwired. This node exists so it can also be fed to the generic nodes - a comparison, a list, a subgraph parameter - which know nothing about that fallback.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_at_pos.desc.1: Only finds MBD machines; an ordinary block or a foreign block entity reports found = false.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_at_pos.desc.2: The level falls back to this machine's, so reaching a neighbour is one Offset node away rather than a level wire plus an offset.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_trait.desc.1: The name is the one shown in the machine editor's trait list. The first trait of a kind keeps its type name; later ones of the same kind are suffixed.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_trait.desc.2: Feed the result to Trait Item Handler, Trait Fluid Handler or Trait Energy Storage to actually read or move its contents.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_traits.desc.1: In the order the definition lists them, which is the order they appear in the machine editor.
A node rather than an implicit conversion because the answer can be no: the same blueprint may be attached to a controller and to a plain machine, and isController is how it tells.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_as_part.desc.1: The part counterpart of As Multiblock Controller, with the same reasoning.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_set_state.desc.1: Goes through the machine's own state change, so it fires State Changed - including back into this blueprint. Setting the state the machine is already in does nothing and fires nothing.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_set_state.desc.2: A name the definition does not declare is ignored rather than throwing.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_set_front_facing.de: Ignored when the direction is not valid for this machine - a machine restricted to the horizontal will not accept up or down.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_set_tier.desc.1: The override is saved with the machine. A negative value clears it, returning the machine to the tier its definition configures. It is server-side state and is not sent to clients.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_set_runtime_bool.de: A definition is shared by every placed block of its type, so editing it changes them all and persists nowhere. This writes the machine's own override instead: saved with the block entity, and reverted by Clear Runtime Value. Overrides are server-side state and are not sent to clients.
Prefer the dedicated nodes - Set Auto IO Enabled and friends - where one exists. This is the escape hatch for the values that do not have one.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_set_runtime_int.des: The numeric counterpart of Set Runtime Value (Boolean); the same override rules apply.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_set_runtime_io.desc: The IO counterpart of Set Runtime Value (Boolean); the same override rules apply.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_clear_runtime_value: Clearing is not the same as writing the definition's current value: a cleared value keeps following the definition, so a later edit in the machine editor reaches this machine too.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_clear_all_runtime_v: Clears every override on the machine, or on one trait when a trait name is given.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_set_auto_io_enabled: Only affects traits that do auto IO - item slots, fluid tanks, energy storages. Others are ignored.
The six side directions and the interval keep reading the definition, so switching auto IO back on restores exactly what the definition configured.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_set_auto_io_side.de: The side is absolute, and is resolved against the machine's current facing - the same way the machine editor's per-side auto IO is.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_set_auto_io_interva: Clamped to at least one tick.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_set_capability_io_s: This is the capability the block exposes to its neighbours, not the auto IO it performs itself. Setting a side to None leaves the capability present but unable to insert or extract.
Neighbouring pipes cache what they resolved, so the change invalidates their caches for you.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_clear_tier.desc.1: The same as Set Machine Tier with a negative value.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_is_runtime_value_ov: For a blueprint that wants to override something only once, or to show players where a machine differs from its definition.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_set_custom_data.des: Replaces the whole tag rather than merging, because that is what makes the change visible: the tag is tracked by identity, so an in-place edit would neither sync nor fire Custom Data Updated.
Use Merge Custom Data to keep the keys already there.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_merge_custom_data.d: Merges keys in, replacing those that collide and leaving the rest. Equivalent to reading Custom Data, merging, and calling Set Custom Data - just without the round trip.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_schedule_render_upd: For a renderer whose look depends on something the game cannot see changing - custom data, a blueprint variable.
Runs on either side. On the server it reaches tracking clients through the usual block update.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_notify_block_update: The heavier hammer: it syncs the block state and pokes every neighbour, so comparators and observers react. Schedule Render Update alone does not.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_mark_dirty.desc.1: Only needed when a blueprint changes something the machine does not already track - the trait and custom-data nodes mark it themselves.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_play_state_sound.de: Plays the looping sound the named machine state defines, and stops on its own when the machine leaves that state.
Client-side only, and refused on the server rather than silently doing nothing there. Put it downstream of Client Tick or a client-side State Changed.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_trigger_anim.desc.1: Safe from either side: on the server it is relayed to every tracking client, on the client it plays locally. Triggering it from Machine Tick is the usual way to make every player see the same animation.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_trigger_anim.desc.2: Leave the controller empty for the model's default controller. The animation name is the one in the animation file.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_play_fx.desc.1: Plays an effect from the machine's Machine FX list, by name. Safe from either side: on the server it is relayed to every tracking client, on the client it plays locally.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_play_fx.desc.2: Only reaches players tracking the chunk right now. An effect that should be visible to whoever turns up later, or survive a relog, belongs on a machine state instead - those start themselves from the state the client already knows.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_play_fx.desc.3: Harmless to fire repeatedly: unless the effect sets Replace Existing, a play call while it is already running does nothing.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_stop_fx.desc.1: Stops an effect started by Play Machine FX. Unknown names do nothing.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_stop_fx.desc.2: Forced Death drops the particles still on screen immediately; leaving it off lets the emitter stop and the particles trail away on their own.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_emit_fx.desc.1: Plays an effect described by its pins rather than picked from the machine's list. Use it when the effect or its placement is computed; otherwise Play Machine FX is authorable and previewable in the editor.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_emit_fx.desc.2: The identifier is the slot the effect occupies. Starting another effect under the same identifier either replaces it or is refused, per Replace Existing - so pick a stable name if you intend to stop it again.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_kill_fx.desc.1: Kills whatever is playing under an identifier, no matter which node or machine state started it.
kg.node.mbd2_redstone_get_signal.desc.1: The weak signal, which is what dust or a comparator beside the machine sees. Set it with Set Redstone Signal.
The strong signal, which powers a block through another - the difference between a torch on the block and dust next to it.
What a comparator reads. Independent of the two side signals.
kg.node.mbd2_redstone_can_connect.desc.1: Follows the signal-connection settings in the machine's basic settings, which are stated relative to the machine's facing rather than to world directions.
kg.node.mbd2_redstone_set_signal.desc.1: Re-notifies the neighbours, so no follow-up Notify Block Update is needed.
kg.node.mbd2_redstone_set_signal.desc.2: Clamped to 0-15 because the machine stores signals as bytes - an out-of-range value would otherwise wrap into a plausible-looking wrong strength.
Same clamping and notification as Set Redstone Signal.
Same clamping and notification as Set Redstone Signal.
kg.node.mbd2_redstone_update_signal.desc: For when something else changed what the neighbours should see - a facing change, a state change - without a signal value moving.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_info.desc.1: Wire the recipe logic once and stack the property blocks inside. With the target unwired it reads the blueprint's own machine's.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_status.desc.1: The raw value. For a condition, the four Is... blocks read better - Branch(Is Working) is one wire where a comparison is three nodes.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_is_working.des: True only while progress is actually advancing.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_is_idle.desc.1: True when nothing matched. A machine with no inputs sits here.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_is_waiting.des: A recipe matched but something stops it - missing inputs, full outputs, not enough energy. Waiting Reason says which.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_is_suspend.des: Switched off, by Set Working Enabled or by something else. The recipe and its progress are kept.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_is_active.desc: Working, waiting, or suspended with a recipe in progress - i.e. the machine has something on the go. The usual driver for a running animation or a lit texture.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_waiting_reason: The same text the machine's hover tooltip shows. Absent while the machine is not waiting.
Counts up in ticks. Zero when nothing is running.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_max_progress.d: The running recipe's duration, after modifiers. Zero when nothing is running, so guard before dividing by it.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_progress_perce: Already handles the zero-duration case, which is why it is here rather than left as a division.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_running_time.d: Counts ticks since the machine last went idle, so it survives across recipes but resets when the machine stops.
The value behind a machine that gets faster the longer it runs.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_last_recipe.de: The recipe as the machine actually runs it - after the definition's modifiers and after any blueprint changed it.
Not something the recipe manager knows about, so its id is not a datapack recipe id. Use Origin Recipe Id for that.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_origin_recipe_: The id the recipe had before anything modified it, which is the one that appears in the datapack and in JEI.
This is what to compare against when a blueprint has to know which recipe is running.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_need_fuel.desc: Comes from the recipe type, not from what the machine is holding.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_fuel_time.desc: Counts down. Zero when nothing is burning.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_fuel_percent.d: Handles the zero-duration case, like Progress Percent.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_last_fuel_reci: The fuel recipe currently burning, which is separate from the recipe the machine is working on.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_set_status.des: Blunt: it does not check that the status makes sense for what the machine is holding, so it can leave the logic in a state it would not have reached on its own.
Prefer Set Working Enabled, Interrupt Recipe or Set Waiting - each of those puts the logic into a consistent state.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_set_working_en: Off suspends the machine, keeping the recipe and its progress; on resumes that recipe if there is one and goes idle otherwise.
This is the node a redstone-controlled machine wants - it is the same path the machine's own on/off uses.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_set_waiting.de: The reason shows as the machine's hover text, so it is worth writing for a player rather than for a developer.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_interrupt.desc: Keeps the progress, so the machine resumes where it left off once whatever stopped it clears.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_reset.desc.1: Throws the recipe and its progress away. Use Interrupt Recipe when the machine should resume.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_mark_dirty.des: The machine caches the modified recipe, so a blueprint that changes something a Recipe Modify hook reads will not be noticed until the next recipe unless this is called.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_set_progress.d: Clamped to zero and below. Setting it past the duration does not finish the recipe - the logic still has to tick.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_set_duration.d: Changes how long the running recipe still takes. To change a recipe before it starts, use Set Recipe Duration under Recipe Modify.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_info.desc.1: Wire the recipe once and stack the property blocks inside.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_info.desc.2: With the target unwired it reads the machine's running recipe. Under a Recipe Modify event, wire the event's recipe instead - the machine's running recipe is the previous one at that point.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_id.desc.1: For a modified recipe this is the original's id with a suffix, so it is not a datapack recipe id. Use Origin Recipe Id on the recipe logic for that.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_duration.desc.1: In ticks, after whatever modifiers have already run.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_priority.desc.1: Only matters when several recipes match the same inputs.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_type.desc.1: The recipe type the recipe belongs to, which may differ from the machine's when the machine proxies another type.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_data.desc.1: Free-form, authored in the recipe editor. This is how a recipe author and a blueprint talk to each other - put a value on the recipe there, read it here.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_data.desc.2: It survives copies, so a blueprint can also write to it with Set Recipe Data and read it back later in the same recipe's life.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_is_modified.desc.1: True once a definition modifier or another blueprint has changed the recipe. Useful for making a modifier idempotent.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_is_xei_hidden.desc.1: From the recipe's own setting, not from anything the machine does.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_has_tick.desc.1: True when the recipe consumes or produces something every tick, as opposed to only at its start and end - the difference between a power drain and a cost.
kg.node.mbd2_content_modifier.desc.1: The unit is multiplier 1, addition 0, which every node that takes a modifier treats as leave it alone.
kg.node.mbd2_content_modifier.desc.2: The same object the definition's own recipe modifiers use, so a blueprint and the editor express changes the same way.
kg.node.mbd2_content_modifier_merge.desc: Not commutative - A is applied first - so swapping the inputs turns doubling-then-adding-one into adding-one-then-doubling.
kg.node.mbd2_content_modifier_apply.desc: For arithmetic elsewhere in the graph that should follow the same rule as the recipe's contents, so the two cannot drift apart.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_copy.desc.1: Always copy before changing. A recipe reaching a Recipe Modify hook may be the shared instance the recipe manager holds, and changing that in place would change the recipe for every machine in the world.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_scale.desc.1: The usual way to make a machine cheaper, faster or more productive. Target picks the side: IN for costs, OUT for products, BOTH for a straight parallel.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_scale.desc.2: modifyDuration additionally scales the duration by the same modifier - which for a parallel is usually not what you want, since a parallel should take the same time.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_set_duration.desc.1: Clamped to at least one tick. For scaling rather than setting, use Scale Recipe with modifyDuration on.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_set_priority.desc.1: For a blueprint that wants its modified recipe to win a tie against another that matches the same inputs.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_set_data.desc.1: Replaces the tag. Read it back with Recipe Data.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_deep_copy.desc.1: Only needed when something downstream mutates a content in place. Scaling and replacing whole contents are both safe on a plain Copy Recipe, which is much cheaper.
kg.node.mbd2_trait_item_handler.desc.1: Once a trait is an item handler, KilaGraph's container nodes work on it unchanged - so a graph that reads a machine's slots is the same graph that reads a chest's.
kg.node.mbd2_trait_item_handler.desc.2: The IO input picks which face of the trait to look at, because a trait can expose different contents for insertion and extraction. BOTH is the unrestricted view.
kg.node.mbd2_trait_fluid_handler.desc.1: Feeds KilaGraph's fluid container nodes, which already cover reading, filling and draining.
kg.node.mbd2_trait_energy_storage.desc.1: Feeds the Energy nodes in this group.
kg.node.mbd2_trait_definition.desc.1: The definition carries the name and the settings the machine editor configured - slot count, capacity, filters.
kg.node.mbd2_item_insert.desc.1: Tries every slot in order, so a partial insert spreads across them.
kg.node.mbd2_item_insert.desc.2: The remainder is what did not fit, and that is the value to feed onward - not the original stack.
kg.node.mbd2_item_insert_slot.desc.1: Use this when which slot matters. Insert Item is the one that just needs the items in somewhere.
kg.node.mbd2_item_extract_slot.desc.1: Returns what was actually available, which may be less than asked for and may be empty.
kg.node.mbd2_item_set_slot.desc.1: Bypasses the slot's filter and its stack limit, so it can put things in a slot no insert would accept.
kg.node.mbd2_item_set_slot.desc.2: Only works on a handler that admits it - MBD2's own item traits do, an arbitrary modded container may not. Check the applied output rather than assuming.
kg.node.mbd2_item_is_valid.desc.1: Asks the slot's filter, not whether there is room. A full slot still reports its item as valid.
kg.node.mbd2_item_slots.desc.1: Every other item node takes a slot index; this is what makes one safe to compute rather than hardcode.
kg.node.mbd2_item_slot_limit.desc.1: The slot's own limit, which the machine editor can set below the item's max stack size.
kg.node.mbd2_energy_info.desc.1: Reports everything about the buffer in one node, so a graph reading two of them does not need six nodes.
kg.node.mbd2_energy_receive.desc.1: Returns how much actually fit, which is how a graph notices a full buffer without asking first.
kg.node.mbd2_energy_extract.desc.1: Returns how much was actually available. Run it with simulate on first when the graph must not take a partial amount.
kg.node.mbd2_multiblock_is_formed.desc.1: False, with isController false, for a machine that is not a controller at all - so the same blueprint can be attached to both kinds without failing on one.
Distinct from Is Formed: a structure can be formed but held invalid, and this is the check the recipe logic itself uses.
The one to gate on when the question is really is this machine allowed to run.
kg.node.mbd2_multiblock_parts.desc.1: In no guaranteed order. Iterate with the generic list nodes.
kg.node.mbd2_multiblock_part_positions.d: A separate node from Multiblock Parts because the positions are usually what a graph wants, and going from a part to its position otherwise needs a step the graph has no node for.
kg.node.mbd2_multiblock_part_machine.des: The bridge back to the machine nodes, so a graph can read a part's traits or state.
kg.node.mbd2_multiblock_error.desc.1: The same text the multiblock preview shows, plus where the check failed - which is what to put in front of a player wondering why their structure will not form.
kg.node.mbd2_multiblock_error.desc.2: Absent while the structure is fine.
kg.node.mbd2_multiblock_part_controllers: A shared part can serve more than one controller, which is why this is a list.
kg.node.mbd2_multiblock_check_pattern.de: The controller only re-checks its pattern every few ticks, so this is what to call after a blueprint changes a block the pattern depends on.
It takes the controller's lock and gives up rather than blocking, so it is safe to call every tick.
kg.node.mbd2_mek_chemical_handler.desc.1: Only present when Mekanism is installed. The trait has to be a chemical tank trait; anything else reports found = false.
kg.node.mbd2_mek_chemical_tank.desc.1: Reports the stack, its amount and the tank's capacity together, so a fill ratio needs no second node.
kg.node.mbd2_mek_chemical_tanks.desc.1: Use it to bound a loop over the tanks.
kg.node.mbd2_mek_chemical_insert.desc.1: Chooses its own tank. The remainder is what did not fit.
kg.node.mbd2_mek_chemical_extract.desc.1: Takes from one named tank rather than choosing, because which chemical comes out matters.
kg.node.mbd2_mek_heat_handler.desc.1: Only present when Mekanism is installed.
kg.node.mbd2_mek_heat_info.desc.1: Heat capacity is how much heat it takes to move the temperature, which is what makes a temperature change computable.
kg.node.mbd2_mek_heat_add.desc.1: A negative value takes heat away. The temperature that results depends on the capability's heat capacity.
kg.node.mbd2_pnc_air_handler.desc.1: Only present when PneumaticCraft is installed.
kg.node.mbd2_pnc_air_info.desc.1: Pressure is derived from the stored air and the buffer's volume, so all three are reported together.
kg.node.mbd2_pnc_add_air.desc.1: A negative value vents air. Adding past the buffer's safe pressure is how a machine explodes, so check the pressure first.
kg.node.mbd2_pnc_heat_handler.desc.1: Only present when PneumaticCraft is installed.
kg.node.mbd2_pnc_heat_info.desc.1: Temperature is in kelvin. Thermal resistance says how readily heat flows in and out.
kg.node.mbd2_pnc_add_heat.desc.1: A negative value takes heat away.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_set_tier.in.tier: The new tier. Negative clears the override.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_set_runtime_bool.in: The trait to act on, by the name shown in the machine editor's trait list. Leave empty to act on the machine itself.
The trait to act on, by the name shown in the machine editor's trait list. Leave empty to act on the machine itself.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_set_runtime_io.in.t: The trait to act on, by the name shown in the machine editor's trait list. Leave empty to act on the machine itself.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_clear_runtime_value: The trait to act on, by the name shown in the machine editor's trait list. Leave empty to act on the machine itself.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_clear_all_runtime_v: The trait to act on, by the name shown in the machine editor's trait list. Leave empty to act on the machine itself.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_set_auto_io_enabled: The trait to act on, by the name shown in the machine editor's trait list. Leave empty to act on the machine itself.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_set_auto_io_side.in: The trait to act on, by the name shown in the machine editor's trait list. Leave empty to act on the machine itself.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_set_auto_io_interva: The trait to act on, by the name shown in the machine editor's trait list. Leave empty to act on the machine itself.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_set_capability_io_s: The trait to act on, by the name shown in the machine editor's trait list. Leave empty to act on the machine itself.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_set_runtime_bool.in: The value's name, for example auto_io.interval, capability_io.top or machine_level.
The value's name, for example auto_io.interval, capability_io.top or machine_level.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_set_runtime_io.in.k: The value's name, for example auto_io.interval, capability_io.top or machine_level.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_clear_runtime_value: The value's name, for example auto_io.interval, capability_io.top or machine_level.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_set_auto_io_side.in: The side to configure, in absolute world directions.
Which way things move on that side. None switches the side off.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_set_auto_io_interva: How many ticks between auto IO runs.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_set_capability_io_s: The side to configure, in absolute world directions.
How neighbours may use the capability on that side.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_is_runtime_value_ov: The trait to act on, by the name shown in the machine editor's trait list. Leave empty to act on the machine itself.
The value's name, for example auto_io.interval, capability_io.top or machine_level.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_trigger_anim.in.con: Which animation controller. Leave empty for the default.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_play_fx.in.name: The effect's name, from the machine's Machine FX list.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_stop_fx.in.name: The effect's name, from the machine's Machine FX list.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_stop_fx.in.forcedDe: Drop the particles still on screen immediately, instead of letting them trail away.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_emit_fx.in.identifi: The slot this effect occupies. Effects with the same identifier replace each other; pass it to Kill Photon FX to stop this one.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_emit_fx.in.fxLocati: The Photon effect id, as namespace:path - for example photon:example. No fx/ prefix and no .fx suffix.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_emit_fx.in.offset: Offset from the centre of the machine's block.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_emit_fx.in.delay: Ticks to wait before the effect starts.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_emit_fx.in.forcedDe: Drop the particles still on screen immediately, instead of letting them trail away.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_emit_fx.in.replaceE: Restart the effect if one is already playing under this identifier. Off means the running one wins.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_kill_fx.in.identifi: The identifier the effect was started under.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_kill_fx.in.forcedDe: Drop the particles still on screen immediately, instead of letting them trail away.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_every_n_ticks.in.in: How many ticks between firings. Twenty is one second. Zero or less never fires.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_every_n_ticks.out.v: True on the ticks that land on this machine's phase of the interval.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_info.in.target: What to read. Leave unwired to read the value derived from this blueprint's own machine.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_at_pos.in.level: Which level. Leave unwired for this machine's.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_at_pos.out.found: False when the trait or capability could not be resolved.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_trait.in.machine: Which machine to act on. Leave unwired for this blueprint's own machine.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_trait.in.name: The name to look up.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_trait.out.trait: The trait, or nothing if the machine has none by that name.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_trait.out.found: False when the trait or capability could not be resolved.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_traits.in.machine: Which machine to act on. Leave unwired for this blueprint's own machine.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_as_controller.in.ma: Which machine to act on. Leave unwired for this blueprint's own machine.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_as_controller.out.c: The machine as a multiblock controller.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_as_controller.out.i: False for a machine that is not a multiblock controller.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_as_part.in.machine: Which machine to act on. Leave unwired for this blueprint's own machine.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_as_part.out.part: The machine as a multiblock part.
kg.node.mbd2_machine_as_part.out.isPart: False for a machine that is not a multiblock part.

kg.node.mbd2_multiblock_is_formed.in.mac: Which machine to act on. Leave unwired for this blueprint's own machine.
kg.node.mbd2_multiblock_is_formed.out.is: False for a machine that is not a multiblock controller.
Which machine to act on. Leave unwired for this blueprint's own machine.

kg.node.mbd2_multiblock_error.in.machine: Which machine to act on. Leave unwired for this blueprint's own machine.

kg.node.mbd2_multiblock_error.out.error: Why it failed - the same text the multiblock preview shows.

kg.node.mbd2_recipe_copy.out.result: The new recipe. Feed it to Set Event Recipe.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_scale.in.modifyDurat: Also scale the recipe's duration by the same modifier.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_scale.out.result: The new recipe. Feed it to Set Event Recipe.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_set_duration.out.res: The new recipe. Feed it to Set Event Recipe.

kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_set_working_en: On resumes the machine, off suspends it.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_set_waiting.in: The text the UI shows while waiting.
kg.node.mbd2_recipe_logic_info.in.target: What to read. Leave unwired to read the value derived from this blueprint's own machine.

kg.node.mbd2_energy_info.out.canReceive: Whether energy can be pushed in.
kg.node.mbd2_energy_info.out.canExtract: Whether energy can be pulled out.
kg.node.mbd2_energy_receive.in.storage: The energy buffer to act on.

kg.node.mbd2_ae2_me_storage.tooltip: A trait's view of the AE2 network it is connected to.
kg.node.mbd2_ae2_me_storage.desc.1: Only an ME interface or pattern provider trait exposes one; anything else reports found = false.
kg.node.mbd2_ae2_me_storage.desc.2: The network has to be online and the trait connected for this to resolve.
kg.node.mbd2_ae2_me_storage.in.trait: The trait to read. Leave unwired and give a name instead.
kg.node.mbd2_ae2_me_storage.in.traitName: The trait's name, as shown in the machine editor's trait list.
kg.node.mbd2_ae2_me_storage.in.io: Which face of the trait to look at. BOTH is the unrestricted view.
kg.node.mbd2_ae2_me_storage.out.found: False when the trait or capability could not be resolved.
kg.node.mbd2_ae2_count.tooltip: How many of an item the network holds.
kg.node.mbd2_ae2_count.desc.1: Answered by a simulated extraction rather than by listing the network, because listing materialises the whole inventory - fine once in a GUI, ruinous on a node that runs every tick.
kg.node.mbd2_ae2_count.desc.2: Counts only exactly matching items, components included.
kg.node.mbd2_ae2_count.in.storage: The ME network to act on.
kg.node.mbd2_ae2_insert.tooltip: Push items into the network. Reports how many were accepted.
kg.node.mbd2_ae2_insert.desc.1: The remainder is the stack count minus what went in; a full or filtered network accepts less.
kg.node.mbd2_ae2_insert.desc.2: Run it with simulate on first when the graph must not lose the leftovers.
kg.node.mbd2_ae2_insert.in.storage: The ME network to act on.
kg.node.mbd2_ae2_insert.in.simulate: Run the arithmetic without changing anything, to ask whether it would work.
kg.node.mbd2_ae2_insert.out.next: Fires after the action, whether or not it applied.
kg.node.mbd2_ae2_extract.tooltip: Pull items out of the network. Reports how many were actually available.
kg.node.mbd2_ae2_extract.desc.1: Returns a count, not a stack - build one with the amount if you need to move it on.
kg.node.mbd2_ae2_extract.desc.2: Simulate answers whether the network could supply the amount without taking it.
kg.node.mbd2_ae2_extract.in.storage: The ME network to act on.
kg.node.mbd2_ae2_extract.in.amount: How much to move, at most.
kg.node.mbd2_ae2_extract.in.simulate: Run the arithmetic without changing anything, to ask whether it would work.
kg.node.mbd2_ae2_extract.out.next: Fires after the action, whether or not it applied.
kg.node.mbd2_aura_in_area.tooltip: How much aura an area holds, and over how many spots.
kg.node.mbd2_aura_in_area.desc.1: Aura lives in the world rather than in the machine, so this takes a position; both it and the level fall back to the machine's own.
kg.node.mbd2_aura_in_area.desc.2: The spot count matters as much as the total: aura spread thin over many spots drains differently from the same amount concentrated.
kg.node.mbd2_aura_in_area.in.level: Which level. Leave unwired for this machine's.
kg.node.mbd2_aura_in_area.in.pos: The position to look at. Leave unwired for this machine's.
kg.node.mbd2_aura_in_area.in.radius: How far around the position to look, in blocks.
kg.node.mbd2_aura_in_area.out.spots: How many aura spots the area has.
kg.node.mbd2_aura_drain.tooltip: Take aura out of an area, from its most aura-rich spot.
kg.node.mbd2_aura_drain.desc.1: The same spot-picking the aura trait uses, so a blueprint and a recipe drain a region the same way rather than fighting over different spots.
kg.node.mbd2_aura_drain.desc.2: Reports what was actually drained, which is less than asked for in a depleted area.
kg.node.mbd2_aura_drain.in.level: Which level. Leave unwired for this machine's.
kg.node.mbd2_aura_drain.in.pos: The position to look at. Leave unwired for this machine's.
kg.node.mbd2_aura_drain.in.radius: How far around the position to look, in blocks.
kg.node.mbd2_aura_drain.in.amount: How much to move, at most.
kg.node.mbd2_aura_drain.out.next: Fires after the action, whether or not it applied.
kg.node.mbd2_aura_store.tooltip: Put aura into an area, at its most depleted spot.
kg.node.mbd2_aura_store.desc.1: The mirror of Drain Aura, and it picks the lowest spot for the same reason.
kg.node.mbd2_aura_store.in.level: Which level. Leave unwired for this machine's.
kg.node.mbd2_aura_store.in.pos: The position to look at. Leave unwired for this machine's.
kg.node.mbd2_aura_store.in.radius: How far around the position to look, in blocks.
kg.node.mbd2_aura_store.in.amount: How much to move, at most.
kg.node.mbd2_aura_store.out.next: Fires after the action, whether or not it applied.
